messages:
ashley (acct-exec): Low-priority alert became blocker. POC integration fails JSON.parse intermittently when using function-calling + json_mode (non-streaming). They pasted a raw response with trailing bytes. Can we triage?

sam (sales-engineer): Short ask: raw HTTP response + headers, and do they reuse connections / do client retries?

ashley (acct-exec): They said keep-alive + client retries on 429/500. Example they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"choices":[{"message":{"name":"extract","arguments":"{\"id\":321}"}}]}
--garbage--
```

tyler (ml-eng): Likely TCP boundary concatenation when a retry happens on the same connection. Need X-Request-Id to map to worker logs.

prashant (infra): Ops-bot pull traces. Short mitigation to give customer: 1) small client sanitizer that extracts the first JSON object before parse, 2) disable aggressive client retries or use SDK idempotency.

ops-bot: Found traces: req_poc_77 -> worker-3. Worker log shows WARN "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes" at 2026-03-22T11:02:14Z.

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN matches a stream flush edge. Quick engineering plan: append a canonical delimiter for json_mode responses in the worker shim to make concatenation detectable. Patch + unit tests ~1.5h, staging ~1.5-2h, 10% canary afterward.

sam (sales-engineer): Customer also asked pricing impact if they stop client retries. Quick blurb?

prashant (infra): One-liner: duplicate retries can increase token spend roughly proportional to retry rate (e.g., 10% retry -> ~10% more tokens). SDK de-dup or idempotency avoids double charges.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell the customer hotfix planned, offer the sanitizer snippet and pricing note, and schedule an immediate call. Will share X-Request-Ids when they respond. :thumbsup:
